thread:
marta: quick sync — need to align Python/TS/Go SDK paging + streaming ergonomics. users hit confusion and some test flakes.
kevin: +1. what's diverging?
marta: python returns async iterator of items, TS returns async generator of pages (user flattens), Go exposes explicit PageToken flow. retries differ too: python retries the whole call, TS retries per-page.
oz: yikes. we should pick a consistent primary surface: item-level iteration for convenience, page helpers opt-in.
samir: fine UX, but remember transports: some routes are streaming-only (gRPC) for latency. we need an adapter model that normalizes page/unary vs stream without hiding important transport guarantees.
marta: proposal: add a tiny client runtime adapter layer. two primitives: PaginatedCall and StreamedCall. both present an Iterable<Item> to the SDK surface. runtime adapters handle token/resume/retries.
kevin: show a sketch?
marta: Python pseudocode: ```class PaginatedAdapter:
    def __init__(self, page_call, retry):
        self._page_call = page_call
        self._retry = retry
    async def __aiter__(self):
        token = None
        while True:
            page = await self._retry.call(lambda: self._page_call(token))
            for it in page.items:
                yield it
            if not page.next_token:
                break
            token = page.next_token``` TS will mirror this returning AsyncIterable<Item>.
oz: key is a well-defined retry boundary. adapter owns page fetch retries. streaming transports keep connection-level reconnects but must not double-retry application-level work. document invariants.
samir: also decide default duplication semantics. my take: default to at-least-once items (simpler). provide an opt-in at-most-once via idempotency tokens and stable resume tokens from backend.
kevin: tests will need to inject mid-page failures and validate ordering/dup suppression. I'll add flaky-resume harness.
marta: telemetry: emit events for page_fetch {token, lat, retries} and stream_reconnect. Console needs token-level cost/latency breakdown.
devops-bot: rollout note: new adapter feature flagged; experimental for 2 weeks.
kevin: SDK surface changes plan:
- Python: add items() async iterator as primary, keep pages() but mark as advanced/deprecate for one release.
- TS: add paginator.items() to flatten pages; keep pages API.
- Go: introduce Iterator type (Next/Item/Err) that flattens items; keep paged helpers.
oz: ergonomics: short examples are crucial. ensure TS typings work with AsyncIterable for ergonomic for-await-of.
marta: follow-ups:
- runtime: create adapter shim PR (runtime/adapter)
- docs: one-pager describing transport variants, adapter behavior, duplication guarantees
- telemetry: event schema update for page_fetch & stream_reconnect
- rollout: feature flag + canary on Dedicated then Hosted
- backend: ask for resume-token support for at-most-once flows

samir: will ping backend owners tomorrow.
kevin: I'll draft PR and tests.
oz: add config knobs: max_pages_in_flight and prefetch_window (affects batching/latency). we route these later into Optimize.
